text:
incident-bot: ALERT — p95 latency spike detected for /v1/generate in region us-east-1. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~820ms at 21:03 UTC. Impacting hosted customers. Paging SRE oncall: maya.

maya (oncall): picking this up. seeing alerts in datadog. routing rule shows high queue length on gpu-pool-3.

liam (eng-runtime): any deploys in the last 12h?

julia (eng-platform): there was a kernel rollforward image pushed to dedicated base images at 02:10 UTC (kc-6.4.12 -> kc-6.4.13). Only ~30% nodes got it in canary.

maya (oncall): confirming — metrics show p50 ~140ms (small bump) but p95 >> p50. suggests tail issues not steady CPU pressure.

chen (perf): can you capture top/perf on a affected node? suspect scheduling latency or timer change. grabbing a node now: gpu-3a-12.

liam (eng-runtime): logs from proxy show larger request queue and backpressure. snippet: ```ERROR: dispatch delayed 820ms, queue_len=47, batch_wait=600ms```

jordan (sre-lead): customer impact: several hosted tenants reporting slow responses and increased error budgets. support team notified. @support-bot start incident status page.

support-bot: STATUS PAGE: Incident created — Latency spike (p95) in us-east-1. Severity: Sev2. Updates every 15m.

chen (perf): perf counters: high context switches and increased softirq time on affected nodes. `vmstat 1` shows high `si`/`so`? hmm not IO heavy. Also seeing runqueue length spikes: runq-sz average 12 -> peaks 120.

maya (oncall): is this limited to hosted or do Dedicated nodes show same?

liam (eng-runtime): Dedicated pool looks normal. only shared-hosted GPU pool and autoscale nodes affected. kernel image tag lines up with the canary nodes.

julia (eng-platform): rollback plan: we can remove the new kernel from the canary pool and reimage to kc-6.4.12. ETA 20m for a small subset. We can also divert traffic to backup pool in another region as mitigation.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation: 1) trigger traffic shift for critical customers to us-west-2. 2) throttle batch sizes for generation to reduce queuing. 3) start reimage of canary nodes. who's owning each?

liam (eng-runtime): I'll flip the routing policy for critical tenant tags to us-west-2 and enable fallback-model routing. doing now.

jordan (sre-lead): chen + liam pair to collect traces and perf. julia owns reimage. maya own comms to customers and status updates. I'll coordinate postmortem artifacts and timeline.

chen (perf): collecting `perf record -a -g -- sleep 30` on affected node. also running `bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:sched:sched_switch { @[comm] = count(); }'` to see scheduling churn. attaching capture sample: ```# bpftrace sample top keys (truncated) redis 120, python 9800, kubelet 3, qemu 0```

liam (eng-runtime): traces from sleuth show long spans inside the runtime's scheduling loop — span: `runtime/dispatch` grows to 600ms in tail traces. breaking down by child spans shows `gpu-queue-wait` often <50ms but `kernel-sched-wait` ~450ms.

maya (oncall): hypothesis 1: kernel scheduler change in kc-6.4.13 increases wake latency under our workload and causes long tail. hypothesis 2: cpufreq governor change causing cores either turbo down or energy saving causing latency spikes. hypothesis 3: NUMA/migration issue due to new kernel page allocator.

jordan (sre-lead): capture required: - kernel dmesg around incident - perf.data - sleuth/span exports for affected requests - top/htop screenshots - list of nodes with new kernel tag.

julia (eng-platform): reimage of canary nodes initiated (gpu-pool-3 nodes). will take ~25m to cycle. marking node set: gpu-3a-{08..15}.

liam (eng-runtime): traffic shift done for critical tenants. fallback-model enabled for non-critical auto routing. p95 for shifted tenants down to ~140ms within 5m. good sign.

chen (perf): quick diff of perf events between good and bad nodes: cpu-clock and context-switch up 3x, rdpmc counters show increased `cache-misses` ~1.8x — suggests scheduler-induced cache-thrashing/affinity churn.

maya (oncall): support update: "We're experiencing a p95 latency regression in us-east-1 affecting hosted customers. We are mitigating by shifting critical traffic and reimaging a canary set. No data loss. More updates in 15m."

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — reimage started at 21:20 UTC, traffic shift applied at 21:08 UTC.

liam (eng-runtime): interesting trace sample: ```trace/span: id=0x7ff, path=/v1/generate, timings: { dispatch: 620ms, kernel-block: 480ms, gpu-wait: 40ms }``` so kernel-block mapping consistent.

chen (perf): running `perf sched record` to get scheduling latencies. attaching small excerpt: ```sched_wakeup: delta=0.45ms -> 450ms for python worker PID 9800; previous kernel shows 0.8ms typical.```

jordan (sre-lead): next steps: if reimage fixes tail, that's strong signal for kernel-induced regression. if not, we need to look at power/cpufreq and node-level hardware.

julia (eng-platform): can we hot-patch kernel parameters as a faster mitigation? `sysctl kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns` change? I can test on a single node safe canary.

maya (oncall): approve testing kernel sysctl change on gpu-3a-14 only. julia go ahead, report immediate effects to thread.

julia (eng-platform): applying `sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=5000000` on gpu-3a-14. monitoring p95 for that node pool.

liam (eng-runtime): after sysctl tweak small improvement on that node: p95 drop from ~820ms -> ~340ms for that host's traffic. not full recovery but directionally better.

chen (perf): suggests scheduler heuristics are at play. collect `perf record -e sched:*` across nodes for longer window.

maya (oncall): reimage progress: 6/8 nodes done, p95 cluster-wide trending down to ~260ms now. still above normal but much improved.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation progress: traffic shifted, canary reimage in progress, sysctl test shows partial improvement.

jordan (sre-lead): okay—short-term mitigation successful enough to reduce customer impact. let's keep reimaging remaining canary and schedule full rollback of kernel push. Ops: please stop further kernel rollouts until postmortem.

julia (eng-platform): halting the kc-6.4.13 rollout and marking patch blocked. I've filed CL-8942 to revert and schedule full coord with kernel team.

liam (eng-runtime): I'll keep fallback-model routing active for 2 hours and revert if stable.

maya (oncall): final immediate status: page de-escalated to Sev3 at 21:55 UTC. Customers experiencing degraded latency but active mitigation in place. Preparing incident timeline and logs for RCA.

chen (perf): saved artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/2154321000/perf.tar.gz, sleuth traces at s3://redwood-incidents/2154321000/traces.jsonl, bpftrace snapshots at s3://redwood-incidents/2154321000/bpftrace.txt

jordan (sre-lead): action items (assignments): - chen: deep perf analysis + correlation table (due EOD) - julia: root cause coordinator, rollback artifact + rollout gating (due next day) - liam: runtime adjustments + traffic rules writeup (due EOD) - maya: post-incident customer notes + timeline (due EOD)

support-bot: NOTE: customer-facing template drafted at docs.incidents/status/2154321000.md.

maya (oncall): thanks team. saving this thread as incident timeline. will reconvene for RCA sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (partial) — De-escalated to monitoring. Final update pending RCA.

jordan (sre-lead): leave a short blameless note: kernel scheduling heuristics regress tail latency under our workloads; rollback and gating prevented wider impact. we'll validate hypothesis with long run perf tests and coordinate with kernel patch authors.

maya (oncall): uploading dmesg excerpts and sleuth spans to the incident bundle. end of thread.
